intro.caption: Lesson 2-5 — range and interquartile range. Max Maxwell drags Clip Squad into Creator Court, claiming his channel is steadier because both channels have the exact same median of 22 thousand views.

balloons.t: Order in Creator Court! Both channels have a median of 22 thousand views. Who is actually steadier?
Equal medians do NOT mean equal spread! Time to measure range and IQR.
My views hit 95 thousand once! Beat that, Clip Squad!
You also had a 5-thousand flop, Max! Let's check the range of both channels first.

pages.caption: Range = greatest − least. It measures the full span of all the data, so one extreme high or low value stretches it.

balloons.t: Max's 5 and 95 stretched his range to 90. What about the middle 50%?
That's the IQR — Q3 minus Q1! It ignores the wild extremes.
Let's put both spreads on the bench. Range tells the whole story; IQR tells the middle half.
Do not let one viral outlier fool the court!
Final case! Two new teams both have a median of 30. Judge the evidence fairly!
Hey! You're supposed to just look at the biggest range!
Verdict is in! Clip Squad is steadier in both range and IQR!

win.caption: Both range (greatest − least) and IQR (Q3 − Q1) measure spread. The range is stretched by extreme values, while the IQR measures only the middle 50% of the data.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Compute the Range
gates.prompt: Compare the 7-video view counts (in thousands). Clip Squad: 18, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 26. Max: 5, 19, 20, 22, 23, 24, 95.
hints: Conceptual: range measures how far apart the lowest and highest values are across the entire data set.
Procedural: subtract the least value from the greatest value (greatest − least).

items.label: Range of Clip Squad's views (18, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 26):

fb.msg: Range is greatest MINUS least, not greatest plus least.
22 is the median (center), not the range (spread).

items.fbDefault: Subtract the least value (18) from the greatest value (26).

items.label: Range of Max's views (5, 19, 20, 22, 23, 24, 95):

fb.msg: Subtract the least from the greatest: 95 − 5, not 95 + 5.
22 is the median, not the range.

items.fbDefault: Subtract the least value (5) from the greatest value (95).

gates.pass: Exhibit A logged: Clip Squad's range is 8, while Max's range explodes to 90!

gates.title: Gate 2 · Compute the IQR
gates.prompt: Now measure only the middle 50% using IQR = Q3 − Q1. Clip Squad: Q1 = 20, Q3 = 24. Max: Q1 = 19, Q3 = 24.
hints: Conceptual: the interquartile range (IQR) is the width of the box on a box plot — the spread of the middle half of the data.
Procedural: subtract Q1 from Q3 (Q3 − Q1), ignoring the minimum and maximum.

steps: Practice set: Min = 4, Q1 = 10, Median = 15, Q3 = 22, Max = 60.
Ignore 4 and 60 — use only Q1 and Q3.
worked.q: If Q1 = 30 and Q3 = 45, what is the IQR?

fb.msg: 8 is the full range (26 − 18). The IQR is Q3 − Q1.
Subtract Q1 from Q3: 24 − 20, do not add.
90 is Max's full range (95 − 5). The IQR only uses Q3 − Q1.

gates.pass: Exhibit B logged: Clip Squad's IQR is 4, and Max's IQR is 5!

gates.title: Gate 3 · Compare the Spread
gates.prompt: Compare Clip Squad (range 8, IQR 4) and Max (range 90, IQR 5).
hints: Conceptual: extreme values stretch the range, while the IQR stays focused on the middle 50%.
Procedural: check which numbers each measure uses before deciding what is true.

steps: Creator X has range 50 and IQR 6. Most videos sit in a 6-unit band, with one huge viral hit stretching the range.
The IQR is always less than or equal to the range because the middle half sits inside the full set.
worked.q: Can the IQR ever be larger than the range?
worked.a: No — the middle half sits inside the full span

items.q: Why is Max's range (90) so much larger than his IQR (5)?

options.t: Because the extremes (5 and 95) stretch the range, while the middle half (19 to 24) is tight
Because range is always 18 times bigger than IQR
options.fb: There is no fixed multiplier; extreme values stretch the range.

options.t: Because IQR includes the highest value
options.fb: IQR only uses Q1 and Q3, so it ignores extreme values.

items.q: Which statements are TRUE about Clip Squad (range 8, IQR 4) vs Max (range 90, IQR 5)? Select all that apply.

options.t: Clip Squad has a smaller range than Max
Clip Squad has a smaller IQR than Max
Max's middle 50% of videos varies by 90 thousand views
options.fb: 90 is Max's full range. His middle 50% varies by 5 (the IQR).

options.t: Both creators have the exact same median (22)

items.fbMiss: Three of the four statements are true — check range, IQR, and median.
items.fbExtra: 90 is Max's full range, not the spread of his middle 50%.

gates.pass: Cross-examination complete! One viral outlier stretched Max's range, not his middle half.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Deliver the Verdict
gates.prompt: Rule on a second case. Team A: Min 12, Q1 25, Med 30, Q3 35, Max 42 (Range = 30, IQR = 10). Team B: Min 2, Q1 28, Med 30, Q3 32, Max 92 (Range = 90).
hints: Conceptual: a smaller range does NOT guarantee a smaller IQR. Compare IQR to judge the middle 50%.
Procedural: compute Team B's IQR using Q3 − Q1, then compare Team B's IQR to Team A's IQR (10).

steps: Team X has range 20, IQR 14. Team Y has range 80, IQR 6.
Even though Team Y's range is huge, its middle 50% (IQR 6) is much tighter than Team X's (IQR 14).
worked.q: Which team has the steadier middle 50%?

items.label: What is Team B's IQR (Q1 = 28, Q3 = 32)?

fb.msg: 90 is Team B's range (92 − 2). IQR is Q3 − Q1.

items.q: Max's lawyer claims: 'Team A is steadier in the middle 50% because Team A has a smaller range!' Does the evidence support that claim?

options.t: No — Team B's IQR is 4 vs Team A's 10, so Team B's middle 50% is actually steadier
Yes — smaller range always means smaller IQR
options.fb: Not true! Team B has a huge range (90) from two outliers, but a tiny IQR (4).

options.t: No — both teams have the same spread because both medians are 30
options.fb: Equal medians do not mean equal spread.

gates.pass: GAVEL DOWN! The court rules: check both range AND IQR, and never let one outlier decide!

journal.heading: Lesson 2-5 — what Creator Court taught us
rows: Greatest minus least. It measures the full spread of all the data, so extreme values stretch it.
Q3 minus Q1. It measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data and ignores extreme outliers.
Two data sets can have the exact same median while having very different ranges and IQRs.
Use IQR when outliers stretch the range and you want to compare how steady the middle half is.
journal.quote: "One viral spike stretches the range, not the IQR. Case dismissed!" — Nova

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 2-5 (Describe Data by Range and Interquartile Range) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: computing range and IQR, distinguishing full spread from middle-50% spread, and resisting outliers.
standards: Recognize that a measure of center summarizes all values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary
